name: Requirements Management Plan
one_liner: How requirements are gathered, prioritised, approved, traced and validated.
purpose: Defines and documents the requirements management approach, process steps and responsibilities, as well as the tools, techniques and artefacts that will be used. The requirements themselves are documented and managed in separate artefacts (e.g. a requirements matrix). Effective requirements management is a critical success factor, because requirements are the starting point for all project work and principally affect project risk, duration and budget.

fields.what: States the purpose: describe the requirements management process for this project, define the related roles and responsibilities, and specify methodology, standards, tools, techniques and templates.
fields.castor: Requirements management for Project CASTOR — LOS renewal, €8.4 m, 26 months.

fields.what: Requirements management gathers, documents and validates requirements and manages their implementation and change; it runs continuously and relates to quality and change management.
fields.castor: Every success criterion SC1–SC5 must trace to at least one testable requirement.

fields.what: The process may be documented here or as a section of the Project Handbook; tailor it — complete the description or delete activities not applicable to the project.
fields.castor: Kept standalone: 214 requirements and an external platform supplier justify a full plan.

fields.what: Managing changing requirements to configuration items — requirements documentation, Project Work Plan, deliverables — is part of project change management, documented in the Project Change Management Plan.
fields.castor: After 26 Jun 2026 a baselined requirement moves only through the Change Log.

fields.what: With stakeholders, gather requirements and document them clearly with metadata. Techniques: brainstorming, nominal group, interviews, observation, storyboards, prototyping, user stories.
fields.who: PM leads · BA documents · URs contribute
fields.castor: Workshops with loan administrators, Apr–Jun 2026, written up by Ada Lovelace (BA).

fields.what: The team assesses feasibility, consistency and completeness and estimates effort/cost; the PM balances the list against budget and time constraints and proposes to stakeholders.
fields.castor: Must-have scope estimated at 1,050 PD inside the 3,100 PD project envelope.

fields.what: Prioritisation belongs to Step 2. MoSCoW = Must have, Should have, Could have, Won't have. Related and dependent requirements must be given the same priority.
fields.who: PM facilitates · PO and BM agree
fields.castor: 214 requirements baselined: 96 Must, 71 Should, 39 Could, 8 Won't.

fields.what: The PM verifies each requirement against the scope boundaries set in the Project Charter; requirements found out-of-scope are logged as “not in scope”.
fields.castor: SRF-backstop screens logged “not in scope” — Treaty reform not yet in force.

fields.what: Every requirement must be testable on the deliverable, so one or more acceptance criteria are defined per requirement; they drive development, test plans and final acceptance.
fields.castor: REQ-042: reconciliation matches the treasury ledger same day, zero manual entries.

fields.what: PM and key stakeholders (PO, BM) negotiate and agree requirements and priorities within the Charter's cost and schedule limits; approval is logged in the Decision Log or MoM.
fields.castor: DEC-004 — baseline approved by Florence Nightingale at the PSC of 26 Jun 2026.

fields.what: PM continuously monitors PCT implementation; new or changed requirements go through formal change control, re-run steps 1–3, and then the Project Work Plan is updated.
fields.castor: Weekly requirements burn-down reviewed with Gustave Eiffel, Levallois's project manager.

fields.what: User Representatives validate the deliverable against each requirement's acceptance criteria and judge whether the business need is met; formal acceptance follows the Deliverables Acceptance Plan.
fields.castor: Marie Curie validates reconciliation requirements in the parallel run, Jan–Apr 2028.

fields.what: Six normal states: Specified, Proposed (passed evaluation), Approved (by the client), Incorporated (into the Work Plan), Implemented (built and tested), Validated (formally accepted).
fields.who: PM defines states · BA maintains them
fields.castor: REQ-042 reached Validated on 30 Apr 2028, at the end of the parallel run.

fields.what: For Fixing at any stage if a requirement is poorly documented, inconsistent or only partly validated; Rejected if obsolete, out of scope, infeasible, postponed, merged or duplicate.
fields.castor: REQ-108 (SRF screens) set Rejected — postponed to a later project.

fields.what: Role-by-role text: PO accountable and approves; BM consulted and names the User Representatives; PM responsible; PCT may supply a business analyst; PSC, SP and AGB informed.
fields.castor: BM Grace Hopper names Marie Curie and two loan administrators as URs.

fields.what: Two rows — the Requirements Management Plan and the Manage Requirements process — both scoring I, I, A, C, C, I, R, S across the eight roles.
fields.castor: PO Florence Nightingale accountable, PM responsible, Project Core Team supports.

fields.what: Lists the techniques used to gather and prioritise requirements — interviews, brainstorming, workshops, observation, prototyping, MoSCoW — and the tools: requirements documentation and traceability matrix.
fields.castor: Workshops, prototyping of the disbursement screen, MoSCoW; matrix kept in Excel.

fields.what: Defines the documentation structure: ID, Name, Category, Type, Description & Details, Acceptance Criteria, Status, Requested by, Identification Date. It is a suggested list; no PM² template exists.
fields.castor: CASTOR requirements catalogue, split by Business, Functional, Technical, Training, Quality.

fields.what: Category groups the requirement (business need, feature, functional, technical, training, quality); Type is the technique used to express it (epic, user story, use case, sketch, business rule).
fields.castor: REQ-042 — Category Functional, Type Use Case, requested by Grace Hopper.

fields.what: Traces high-level business needs down to detailed requirements and on to deliverables. Columns: ID, Name, Status, Priority, Size, Comments, Derived From, Related WBS code, Specification document, Test Plan.
fields.castor: REQ-042 derived from SC2, WBS code 3.4, test plan TP-07.

fields.what: Priority states relative importance (High/Medium/Low, or MoSCoW). Size indicates effort or difficulty of implementation (Big, Medium, Small). They are two separate columns.
fields.castor: REQ-108: Priority Could have, Size Big — the reason it was postponed.

fields.what: Any changed or new requirement must be logged on a Change Request Form, follow the requirements process in section 3, and pass change control per the Handbook or Change Plan.
fields.castor: The cabinet's SRF request was routed as CR-011, not slipped in as a requirement.

fields.what: Names the connected plans: Project Handbook (high-level approach), Project Change Management Plan (change of scope, requirements, budget, schedule), Deliverables Acceptance Plan (acceptance criteria and responsibilities).
fields.castor: Handbook v1.0, Change Plan v1.0 and Deliverables Acceptance Plan v1.0, all 26 Jun 2026.

fields.what: Lists each reference or related document by title, version, date and source or link/location, so the plan stays usable without duplicating other artefacts.
fields.castor: 04.Project_Handbook.CASTOR.26-06-2026.V1.0.docx in the ESM PSO project folder.

traps: The plan says how; the requirements themselves live in separate requirements documents.
Requirements Management Plan is the only Management Plan where PCT = S (Supports).
MoSCoW is priority; Size (Big/Medium/Small) is effort — different matrix columns.
Changing a baselined requirement is a Change Request, not a new requirement.
URs validate implemented requirements; the PM does not, and acceptance follows the Acceptance Plan.
